title: Federal Trade Commission Act of 1914 — Statute profile
subject: Federal Trade Commission Act of 1914
summary: Federal Trade Commission Act of 1914 is a statute of United States enacted in 1914, in the area of consumer protection. Created the Federal Trade Commission to police unfair business practices. It is formally cited as Pub. L. 63-203.
key_points: Core effect: Created the Federal Trade Commission to police unfair business practices.
guidance: General information only, not legal advice. Use the citation to look up the current official text; statutes are amended over time.
